extracted.intended_audience: UK government departments and policy teams responsible for designing and running public consultations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for UK government departments on how to design and run public consultations, emphasising proportionate, accessible, early and digitally-enabled engagement and avoiding unnecessary consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionate and targeted approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting a more proportionate and targeted approach to consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The government is improving the way it consults by adopting a more proportionate and targeted approach — i.e., focus consultation effort where appropriate and avoid blanket or excessive consultations that are not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use digital methods to consult a wider group earlier
rubrics_metrics.description: We will use more digital methods to consult with a wider group of people at an earlier stage in the policy-forming process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use online/digital engagement tools to broaden participation and to engage stakeholders earlier in policy development rather than only at late stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make it easier for the public to contribute their views
rubrics_metrics.description: We will make it easier for the public to contribute their views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove barriers to participation (e.g., provide accessible formats on request — contact accessible.formats@cabinetoffice.gov.uk), simplify submission mechanisms and lower friction so more people can respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear language and plain English in consultation documents
rubrics_metrics.description: We will try harder to use clear language and plain English in consultation documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft consultation documents in plain English and avoid unnecessary jargon so the public can understand the issues and respond meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid consultation fatigue by consulting only on genuinely undecided issues
rubrics_metrics.description: We will reduce the risk of 'consultation fatigue' by making sure we consult only on issues that are genuinely undecided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not consult on matters where decisions have effectively already been made; prioritise consultations where public input can influence outcomes to respect respondents' time and maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be responsive to scrutiny and amend principles based on feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: The principles have been amended in the light of comments from the Secondary Legislation Scrutiny Committee to demonstrate the government’s desire to engage more effectively with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation guidance and practice should be updated when credible external feedback or scrutiny identifies improvements; show responsiveness to oversight and stakeholder comments.
